summary:
What we developed:
ASTRA-HEALTH is an autonomous, full-stack astronaut health monitoring and predictive risk-triage platform designed for long-duration spaceflight. It unites a React operations dashboard, FastAPI backend, and an 85-model machine learning ensemble across 17 bio-medical domains, continuously analyzing 147 biometric, environmental, and operational telemetry parameters.
How it addresses the challenge:
During deep-space voyages to the Moon and Mars, signal latencies and communication blackouts prevent real-time medical intervention from Earth Mission Control. ASTRA-HEALTH solves this by operationalizing NASA’s 5 Spaceflight Hazards and 17 Health Risk Domains directly on-orbit. It automates longitudinal baseline tracking, identifies physiological anomalies, and provides onboard "what-if" risk simulations without requiring continuous ground-link connectivity.
Why it is important:
Deep-space exploration demands a paradigm shift from Earth-dependent telemedicine to autonomous crew healthcare. By delivering transparent, probabilistic risk triage and anatomical telemetry mapping while preserving complete clinical data provenance, ASTRA-HEALTH empowers flight crews to detect subtle health degradation early, mitigate catastrophic medical events, and safeguard mission success beyond Low Earth Orbit.
details:
ASTRA-HEALTH: Project Details

1. What does it do or how does it work?

ASTRA-HEALTH is an integrated astronaut health monitoring and mission decision-support platform designed to solve a fundamental operational dilemma in space medicine: health signals, environmental context, and clinical guidance are fragmented.

The platform connects physiological readings, daily behavioral check-ins, and habitat telemetry into one unified crew-health picture through a 4-stage operational loop:

[ CAPTURE ] ──▶ [ CONNECT ] ──▶ [ INTERPRET ] ──▶ [ ACT ]

Vitals, Sleep, Timestamped Personalized Protocol-Linked

Habitat Logs Relational DB Baselines & ML Actionable Alerts

  1. CAPTURE (Multi-Stream Ingestion):
    • Physiological: Heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation (SpO2SpO_2SpO2​), body temperature, fluid shifts, and sensorimotor markers.
    • Behavioral: Sleep duration and quality, cognitive fatigue, mood, stress scores, and symptom check-ins.
    • Mission Context: Mission day (1–180), flight phase (Outbound, Cruise, Return), radiation dosimeter rates and cabin atmosphere (CO2CO_2CO2​, O2O_2O2​, pressure).
    • Ingests a canonical 147-parameter dataset covering 20 astronauts (AST001–AST020) and 3,600 observation days.
    • Relational database models (SQLite via SQLAlchemy) preserve the strict relationships between astronaut, mission phase, and timestamps, saving the complete 147-column telemetry intact as JSON to eliminate lossy downsampling.
    • Longitudinal Personal Baselines: Rather than comparing an astronaut to generic Earth norms, the rule-based engine benchmarks current readings against that astronaut’s own historical mission baseline.
    • Machine Learning Risk Triage: An ensemble of 85 champion model pipelines (5-fold cross-validation across 17 risk domains: Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Decision Trees) predicts risk classifications (LOW, MODERATE, HIGH) and generates a composite mission status (GREEN, AMBER, RED) with fold-averaged confidence scores.
    • Triggers protocol-aligned early alerts, provides an interactive Body Explorer linking metrics directly to affected organ systems, and offers a "What-If" ML Simulation Workbench where astronauts can adjust telemetry sliders (e.g., simulating radiation spikes or sleep loss) to see how risks evolve.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Eliminates the Ground-Comms Latency Bottleneck: Deep-space travel to the Moon or Mars involves 5- to 22-minute one-way radio delays and total solar conjunction blackouts. ASTRA-HEALTH operates 100% offline and on-orbit, giving the crew autonomous, real-time medical decision support.
  • Solves Signal Fragmentation: Flight surgeons and astronauts no longer have to cross-reference multiple disjointed logs (sleep apps, dosimeter readers, cabin air monitors). Everything converges onto a single mission-control dashboard.
  • Early Detection of Sub-Clinical Trends: By tracking gradual baseline shifts over 180 days, it flags silent degradations—such as the onset of Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS), bone demineralization, or cardiovascular deconditioning—weeks before acute symptoms surface.
  • Low Crew Cognitive Burden: Designed for high-stress operational environments, using clear tri-color triage indicators (GREEN / AMBER / RED) and high-contrast night-shift modes that prevent alert fatigue and information overload.
  • Interactive Countermeasure Testing: Crew members can simulate whether modifying daily resistive exercises or adjusting cabin scrubbers will effectively stabilize an emerging health anomaly before taking physical action.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Making Long-Duration Spaceflight Viable: Deep space has no emergency rooms and no quick abort trajectories. ASTRA-HEALTH establishes the digital infrastructure necessary for human survivability on multi-year missions to Mars and Lunar Artemis bases.
    • Remote polar and Antarctic scientific stations.
    • Submarines and offshore energy platforms.
    • Rural and frontier healthcare clinics and disaster-relief operations where cellular and internet networks have failed.

5. How is your project creative?

  1. Context-Aware Personal Baselines vs. Terrestrial Norms:
    Standard medical software compares patients to hospital averages on Earth—an approach that produces constant false alarms in space, where microgravity-induced cephalad fluid shifts and muscle adaptations are expected. ASTRA-HEALTH creatively calculates health status by comparing an astronaut to their own rolling mission baseline.
  2. Interactive Anatomical Body Explorer:
    Instead of forcing astronauts to decipher complex numerical tables, the platform visually connects 147 raw sensor telemetry streams directly to human physiological systems (cardiovascular, ocular, neurological, musculoskeletal, vestibular), turning data points into immediate spatial understanding.
  3. Transparent, Explainable AI (Anti-Black-Box):
    Rather than using uninterpretable deep neural networks, our ML engine uses vetted champion classifiers that output raw fold-averaged probabilities, confidence scores, and high-risk likelihoods. Astronauts and flight surgeons can see why an assessment was made.
  4. Proactive "What-If" Countermeasure Sandbox:
    It transforms the medical record from a passive historical archive into an active predictive simulation tool, letting astronauts experiment with environmental and lifestyle variables to forecast health outcomes.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team evaluated five critical technical and operational constraints during development:

  1. Zero-Connectivity Architecture (Deep-Space Latency):
    We operated under the strict constraint that the application must run with zero internet or cloud access. All databases, models, and UI assets are hosted locally on the spacecraft’s edge hardware.
  2. Medical Ethics & Scope Boundaries:
    Our guiding design principle: The platform does not diagnose disease or replace flight surgeons, clinical protocols, or validated medical devices. It acts as an operational decision-support tool, using cautious review language rather than prescriptive medical directives.
  3. Crew Cognitive Fatigue & Alert Burden:
    Space crews suffer from sleep deprivation and heavy workloads. We prioritized low-friction daily check-ins, automated data pre-filling, and hierarchical color coding (GREEN / AMBER / RED) to prevent alarm fatigue and enable split-second comprehension.
    • Phase 1 (Foundation): Core workflows, local database, authentication, and baseline tracking (Completed).
    • Phase 2 (Integration): Direct ingestion connectors for flight wearables (e.g., Bio-Monitor smart shirts) and habitat environmental sensors.
    • Phase 3 (Intelligence): Refined ML ensembles with active confidence tracking (Completed in prototype).
    • Phase 4 (Validation): Clinical review of warning thresholds with aerospace medicine experts and astronaut analog test subjects.
    • Phase 5 (Deployment): Operational field testing in Earth-based analog habitats (e.g., HERA, MDRS, CHAPEA).
